standard_prerequisites.name: Minimal numerical types, minus-one and minus-two indices and the elementary bounds
standard_prerequisites.statement: A numerical type is a tuple of an integer and integer families of multiplicities, intersection numbers, weights and genera subject to the five defining conditions of the chapter; it is minimal when it has no minus-one index, that is, no index whose genus is zero and whose self-intersection equals the negative of its weight, and the boundary cases where the diagonal entry is large are collected in the definitions of minus-one and minus-two indices. The chapter's elementary bound on neighbouring entries and its lemmas on the sign of the diagonal entries and on the genus of a neighbouring index supply the estimates the proof uses. The author's own definitions and lemmas of the same chapter are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is the quantitative input of the classification of minimal types: together with the bound on the weighted intersection numbers it makes the heart of the type bounded, which is what makes the enumeration of minimal types of fixed genus finite.

core_obligations: Reduce to one entry of the heart: by the chapter's elementary bound on neighbouring entries it is enough to bound a single distinguished entry of the intersection graph, and the reduction is the first step of the proof (source line 4129).

Use minimality to exclude the minus-one indices, and analyse the remaining boundary cases: the definitions of minus-one and minus-two indices describe exactly the configurations in which the diagonal entry is too large, and the lemmas about the genus of a neighbouring index apply to each of them in turn (source lines 4130-4150).

Compare the contributions with the genus: for each remaining configuration the author derives an inequality between the entry under consideration and the genus of the type, using that the diagonal entries are negative and that the genus is at least two (source lines 4150-4165).
Collect the estimates: the individual inequalities are combined into the stated bound for the heart, which completes the proof (source lines 4165-4169).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the assertion to a bound for one entry of the heart.
Use minimality and the minus-one and minus-two configurations to classify the possible local shapes.
Derive the numerical inequality for each shape against the genus.
Combine the inequalities into the asserted bound.
